correctness.rationale: Every decreasing order-preserving idempotent is exactly a floor map onto its fixed set. A pair fails to commute precisely when a common-point gap contains both exclusive fixed-point colors, as proved by evaluating the composites at a later exclusive fixed point. Gap products yield B/(1-wB); an independent endpoint-bit argument yields each commuting-idempotent centralizer. Rational partial fractions give the count and decay. The self-contained verifier independently composes all idempotent pairs for n<=9, matches each trivariate coefficient and all centralizers, enumerates all Catalan maps for n<=7, and exits VERIFY_OK. Finite checks supplement, rather than replace, the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The finite Catalan monoid is a natural transformation semigroup, and pairwise commutativity of its idempotents is a structurally motivated distinction from the partial-injective i-Catalan variant. The trivariate formula computes every natural fixed-set interaction statistic of commuting ordered pairs for all n, while the centralizer transfer gives individual-idempotent information. The exponential rarity law and linear conditional common-fixed-point scale quantify the obstruction. This family-level refinement is not a routine table lookup, arbitrary slice or mere substitution into a known recurrence.
